privacy.metaDescription: How TrendTraffic processes personal data: what we collect, the legal bases under the GDPR, AI processing of photos and voices, sub-processors, international transfers, retention periods and your rights.

sections.b:

1.2. The Data Controller of the personal data of the Platform's Users is:

(hereinafter, the "Provider").

1.3. This Policy has been drawn up in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation, "GDPR"). It should be read together with the Terms of Service and the Cookie Policy.

2.1. Account data: email address and an encrypted (hashed) password. If you choose "Sign in with Google", we receive your name, email address and profile picture from your Google account.

2.2. Billing data: subscription plan and status, invoicing details and payment history. All card payments are processed directly by the secure payment provider Stripe; the Provider never stores full payment card numbers.

2.3. Integration data (optional, "bring your own key"): API keys and tokens for third-party services that you connect at your own discretion — for example Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, FAL.ai, ElevenLabs, HeyGen, Blotato or TikHub. These keys are stored encrypted at rest and are used exclusively to execute the operations you request.

2.4. Content data: media files and materials that you upload or create on the Platform — including photographs used to create photo avatars, voice recordings used for voice cloning, videos, scripts, subtitles, brand kits and generated clips — as well as your trend queries, product and audience descriptions, keywords, and links to third-party videos you submit for analysis.

2.5. Technical data: IP address, browser type, JWT authorisation tokens and activity logs necessary for security and troubleshooting.

2.6. Publicly available social media data: to provide trend analytics, the Platform retrieves public content and engagement metrics (videos, channels, view/like counts, captions) from TikTok, Instagram and YouTube through the licensed data provider TikHub. This data is obtained from publicly accessible sources rather than from the data subjects themselves; it is processed solely to compute trend and market analytics and is not used to profile or identify the individuals appearing in such content.

sections.h: 3. Purposes and Legal Bases of Processing
sections.b:
The Provider processes personal data for the following purposes and on the following legal bases under Article 6(1) GDPR:

  • Performance of the contract (Art. 6(1)(b)): creating and maintaining your account, providing the Platform's features (trend discovery, video analysis, AI video studio, scheduling and publishing), processing subscription payments and providing technical support.
  • Compliance with legal obligations (Art. 6(1)(c)): accounting, tax and invoicing duties.
  • Legitimate interests (Art. 6(1)(f)): securing the Platform, preventing fraud and abuse, maintaining service stability, keeping privacy-preserving internal service metrics, and processing publicly available social media content for trend analytics.
  • Consent (Art. 6(1)(a)): non-essential cookies and similar technologies (see the Cookie Policy) and any future optional features expressly based on consent. Consent can be withdrawn at any time with effect for the future.

The Platform does not make automated decisions producing legal or similarly significant effects concerning you within the meaning of Article 22 GDPR.

4.1. Photographs and voice recordings that you upload are processed only upon your explicit action and solely to render the specific result you request (for example, a photo avatar or an AI voiceover). They are not used for biometric identification or biometric categorisation of any person, and they are not used by the Provider to train artificial intelligence models.

4.2. Where creating an avatar or a voice clone requires registering the material with a third-party AI provider (for example HeyGen or ElevenLabs), the material is transmitted to that provider strictly for the requested operation and is processed under that provider's terms and data processing agreements.

4.3. You may delete uploaded media and generated assets in the Platform's gallery at any time. Upon deletion of your account, associated content is removed, except where retention is required by law (see Section 7).

4.4. You must hold the necessary rights and consents of any person whose image or voice you upload or clone. The detailed obligations are set out in the Terms of Service.

sections.h: 5. Disclosure of Data to Third Parties (Sub-processors)
sections.b:
To operate the Platform, the Provider engages trusted third-party services that may receive partial access to data under strict contractual arrangements, and only to the extent necessary:

  • Infrastructure and hosting: Hostinger (virtual servers located in the European Economic Area; databases and application code).
  • Payments: Stripe (subscription payments, invoicing, fraud prevention).
  • Artificial intelligence: Google (Gemini models), Anthropic (Claude models), OpenAI, FAL.ai, HeyGen (avatar rendering), ElevenLabs (speech synthesis and voice cloning) — via their official APIs. Only the content necessary for the specific operation you invoke is transmitted.
  • Social media data: TikHub (retrieval of publicly available platform content and metrics).
  • Publishing: Blotato and the social networks you connect (TikTok, Meta/Instagram, YouTube/Google) — they receive the content you schedule for publication and the credentials you have linked in your own accounts.
  • Authentication: Google (optional "Sign in with Google").

Where you connect your own API key or subscription of a third-party service, that service processes your data under your own agreement with it; the Provider merely transmits your requests on your behalf.

The Provider does not sell personal data and does not use it for third-party advertising or marketing purposes.

6.1. The Platform's own databases and application code are hosted on servers located within the European Economic Area (EEA).

6.2. Some of the service providers listed in Section 5 (for example Stripe, Google, Anthropic, OpenAI, HeyGen, ElevenLabs, FAL.ai, Blotato) are established in the United States or other third countries. Transfers to such providers take place on the basis of an adequacy decision of the European Commission (including the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework, where the provider is certified) or on the basis of the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses (Art. 46(2)(c) GDPR) with supplementary measures where required.

6.3. A copy of the relevant safeguards can be requested via the contact email indicated in Section 1.

• Account data: for the duration of the subscription or account activity. Upon account deletion the data is erased, except for information that must be retained to comply with tax and accounting legislation (up to 5 years).
  • Content data (media, analyses, generated videos): until you delete them via the Platform or close your account.
  • Integration keys (BYOK): until you remove them in the settings or close your account; stored encrypted for the entire period.
  • Technical logs: as a rule, no longer than 12 months, unless a longer period is required to investigate security incidents or by law.
  • Payment records: for the periods required by applicable tax law.

8.1. The Provider applies state-of-the-art technical and organisational measures: encrypted data transmission (HTTPS/TLS), hashing of passwords, encryption of stored API keys, JWT-based session protection, access controls and the principle of least privilege.

8.2. Access to personal data is limited to persons who need it to operate the Platform and who are bound by confidentiality obligations.

8.3. In the event of a personal data breach likely to result in a risk to your rights and freedoms, the Provider will notify the competent supervisory authority and, where required by Article 34 GDPR, the affected Users.

You have the right to:

  • request access to your personal data and obtain a copy of it;
  • request rectification of inaccurate or incomplete data;
  • request erasure of data (the "right to be forgotten") where there is no longer a legal ground for retention;
  • request restriction of processing;
  • receive your data in a structured, machine-readable format and have it transmitted to another controller (data portability);
  • object to processing based on legitimate interests, on grounds relating to your particular situation;
  • withdraw consent at any time, without affecting the lawfulness of processing carried out before the withdrawal.

To exercise these rights, send a request to SEO@trendtraffic.pro. The Provider responds within one month (extendable by two further months for complex requests, with notice).

You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority — in Poland, the President of the Personal Data Protection Office (Prezes Urzędu Ochrony Danych Osobowych, UODO, ul. Stawki 2, 00-193 Warszawa, uodo.gov.pl), or with the supervisory authority of your habitual residence.

sections.h: 10. Artificial Intelligence and Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (EU AI Act)
sections.b:
10.1. The Platform integrates publicly available general-purpose AI models of third-party providers via their official APIs (Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, HeyGen, ElevenLabs, FAL.ai) for trend analysis, script and keyword generation, translation, frame-by-frame video analysis, avatar rendering and speech synthesis. The Provider does not develop or train its own AI models and is not a provider of general-purpose AI models within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the "EU AI Act").

10.2. The Platform's AI uses fall within the minimal-risk and limited-risk categories of the EU AI Act. The Platform does not deploy high-risk AI systems within the meaning of Annex III of the Regulation.

10.3. Transparency of synthetic content: the Platform is a tool for creating AI-generated and AI-manipulated video, audio and images (including avatars and cloned voices). AI features are clearly labelled in the interface. Where the underlying AI providers embed machine-readable markings or watermarks into generated content (Article 50(2) of the EU AI Act), the Platform preserves them and does not remove them. Users are contractually obliged to disclose deep fakes and other synthetic content as required by Article 50(4) of the EU AI Act and by the rules of the social networks where they publish (see the Terms of Service).

10.4. Practices prohibited by Article 5 of the EU AI Act — subliminal manipulation, exploitation of vulnerabilities (including those of children), social scoring, predictive assessment of criminal offending of individuals, untargeted scraping of facial images from the internet or CCTV, emotion recognition in the workplace and in education, biometric categorisation based on sensitive attributes, and real-time remote biometric identification in publicly accessible spaces — are not offered by the Platform, are prohibited by the Terms of Service, and requests aimed at such practices are refused.

10.5. Human oversight: AI outputs (analyses, scripts, keywords, generated videos) are drafts that may contain inaccuracies. Users review and approve content before use or publication.

The Platform is a professional tool intended for persons who are at least 18 years old. The Provider does not knowingly collect personal data of children. If you believe that a child has provided personal data to the Platform, please contact SEO@trendtraffic.pro and the data will be deleted.

The Provider may amend this Policy, in particular to reflect changes in law or in the Platform's functionality. The current version is always published on the Platform, with the "last updated" date at the top. In the event of material changes, Users will additionally be notified by email or in the application.

cookies.title: Cookie Policy
cookies.subtitle: of the TrendTraffic platform
cookies.metaDescription: Which cookies and localStorage entries TrendTraffic uses, for what purposes and for how long, which third parties set cookies (Stripe, Google sign-in), and how to give, refuse or change your consent.

sections.h: 1. What Cookies and Similar Technologies Are
sections.b:
1.1. Cookies are small text files stored on your device when you visit a website, allowing the site to recognise your device and remember preferences.

1.2. In addition to cookies, the TrendTraffic platform uses the browser's Local Storage — among other things, to store the authorisation token of your session, your language and interface theme, and your cookie consent choice. This Policy applies to cookies and Local Storage alike.

2.1. Strictly necessary (technical) — required for the Platform to function; they are used on the basis of the Provider's legitimate interest and do not require consent:

  • vibevox_token — the JWT authorisation token of your session (Local Storage; until logout or token expiry);
  • vibevox_user — a cache of the signed-in user's profile (Local Storage; until logout);
  • tt_cookie_consent — stores your cookie consent choice (Local Storage; until you change or clear it).

2.2. Functional (preferences):

  • i18nextLng — the selected interface language (Local Storage; until changed or cleared);
  • vibevox_theme — light/dark theme (Local Storage; until changed or cleared).

For historical reasons, some identifiers carry the "vibevox" prefix of the Provider's earlier product line; they belong to the TrendTraffic platform.

2.3. Analytics: the Platform currently sets no third-party analytics or advertising trackers. Basic, privacy-preserving service metrics are collected server-side without cross-site tracking. If consent-based analytics are ever introduced, they will run only after you choose "Accept all".

2.4. Third-party cookies: external services integrated into the Platform may set their own cookies when you use them:

  • Stripe — payment security and fraud prevention on payment and billing pages (e.g. __stripe_mid, ~1 year; __stripe_sid, ~30 minutes);
  • Google — when you use "Sign in with Google", Google sets cookies under its own policy;
  • Connected social networks (TikTok, Meta/Instagram, YouTube) — only within their own interfaces when you connect or open them.

• Authentication and protection of the User's session.
  • Security of payment transactions.
  • Remembering the language, theme and your consent choice.
  • Ensuring the stability and performance of the service.

4.1. On your first visit, the Platform displays a consent banner in accordance with Article 399 of the Polish Electronic Communications Law (Prawo komunikacji elektronicznej), the GDPR and the ePrivacy Directive (2002/58/EC). You may choose "Accept all" or "Necessary only" — both options are equally accessible, and no non-essential technologies are activated before your choice.

4.2. You can change your choice at any time — use the "Cookie settings" link in the site footer or the button below this Policy; the banner will reopen.

4.3. Most browsers also allow you to block or delete cookies and Local Storage in their settings (Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Safari, Microsoft Edge). Note: if strictly necessary entries are blocked or deleted entirely, signing in and using the Platform will become impossible.

• Session data: deleted on logout or upon expiry of the authorisation token.
  • Preferences (language, theme, consent choice): stored until you change them or clear your browser data; the consent choice is refreshed at least every 12 months by re-display of the banner where required.
  • Third-party cookies: according to the respective provider's policy (see Section 2.4).

Questions about this Cookie Policy can be sent to:

Email: SEO@trendtraffic.pro
Address: LARYSA DANYUK, ul. Jana III Sobieskiego, nr 1, lok. 49, 02-957 Warszawa, Poland.

How personal data is processed is described in the Privacy Policy.
